pr.title: StateTransform: Do not renumber resume local.
pr.description:
MIR parameters are not explicitly assigned-to when entering the MIR body. If we want to save their values inside the coroutine state, we need to do so explicitly.

This was done by renaming the `_2` local, and introducing an explicit assignment pre-transform. This particular trick confuses me.

This version makes explicit that we are assigning parameters to saved locals.

processing.reason:
No source-grounded wrong transformation exists to encode. PR #146552 is explicitly an equivalence-preserving StateTransform refactor, not a bug fix: its tests are only MIR-dump expectation changes (local renumbering, `_s{}` debug names), with no runtime regression and no execution/reproduction claimed.

The historical code's rename+pre-assignment does initialize the saved parameter field: `replace_local(CTX_ARG, ...)` renames `_2` to a fresh local just before liveness/StateTransform runs, and the inserted start assignment `old_resume_local = move _2` is itself rewritten by TransformVisitor into the coroutine-field store when that renamed local is live across a yield. The new code performs the same store explicitly from `_2` after `visit_body`. Thus both variants initialize the saved state field.

The old unconditional resume move is also safe, not a self-move: `RenameLocalVisitor` is run by `replace_local` over the whole body (including Yield terminator places), so a Yield `resume_arg` equal to `_2` has already been renamed before `create_cases` emits `point.resume_arg = move _2`. When the new code sees `point.resume_arg == CTX_ARG`, the guard merely avoids an unnecessary `_2 = move _2`; the old code instead emits the equivalent move into the renamed local/field. The guard is not fixing a historical semantic error.

Constructing a pair that drops the initial parameter store, or that forcibly makes the resume move fail, would manufacture a non-historical bug rather than model the PR's actual old transformation. The only observable differences are MIR local numbering/debug names and the redundant resume move, none of which change program semantics. Therefore no valid original/transformed pair can be validated.

analysis.summary: StateTransform refactor for coroutine parameter saving: keep the resume argument `_2`/CTX_ARG as an actual MIR parameter and explicitly assign any MIR argument remapped into coroutine state, rather than renaming `_2` via replace_local and pre-inserting a dedicated assignment. No execution/reproduction is claimed; this is a source-described MIR-transform refactor, not a confirmed bug fix.
analysis.originalLogic: StateTransform handled the resume argument by replacing/renaming it: the old code did `let resume_local = CTX_ARG;`, `let old_resume_local = replace_local(resume_local, resume_ty, body, tcx);`, then inserted at the start block an assignment from the resume local into the renamed local. At each resume point it unconditionally did `let resume_arg = CTX_ARG;` and emitted an assignment into `point.resume_arg`. The patch's retained comment explains: "This is needed because the resume argument `_2` might be live across a `yield`, in which case there is no `Assign` to it that the transform can turn into a store to the coroutine state. After the yield the slot in the coroutine state would then be uninitialized."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically superseded (not confirmed semantically wrong) transformation renamed the resume local `_2`/CTX_ARG to a fresh local with replace_local, inserted an initial move from CTX_ARG into that renamed local, and at every Resume point moved CTX_ARG into `point.resume_arg` unconditionally. The replacement keeps `_2` unchanged and instead, after `transform.visit_body(body)`, inserts explicit assignments for all MIR arguments whose locals were remapped into coroutine-state fields: `let args_iter = body.args_iter();` and for each `local`, `let (ty, variant_index, idx) = transform.remap[local]?;`, emit `Assign(transform.make_field(variant_index, idx, ty), Move(local))`. Resume handling becomes conditional: `if operation == Operation::Resume && point.resume_arg != CTX_ARG.into()`, then move CTX_ARG into `point.resume_arg`. Thus the corrected transformed MIR contains `debug _task_context => _2;` and an explicit field store such as `(((*_19) as variant#4).0: std::string::String) = move _2;` instead of the renamed-local pass.
analysis.inputDomain: Coroutine-like MIR bodies processed by StateTransform (generators, async fn bodies, async closures), especially bodies with arguments live across suspend/yield points. Includes the simplest coroutine with `_2: u8`, async functions with `_2: &mut Context<'_>`, async closures, plain and `#[track_caller]` coroutine closures, and both panic=abort and panic=unwind configurations. Relevant cases include resume points where `point.resume_arg` equals CTX_ARG (`_2`) and where it differs, and arguments remapped into saved coroutine fields versus arguments not so remapped.
analysis.trigger: StateTransform runs on a body that has a yield type (`body.yield_ty()`), computes the remapping of locals to coroutine fields, and must initialize saved parameter values because the patch states: "MIR parameters are not explicitly assigned-to when entering the MIR body. If we want to save their values inside the coroutine state, we need to do so explicitly." The issue manifests whenever a parameter such as the resume argument `_2` is live across a yield/suspend point or is otherwise saved into coroutine state; the state field needs an explicit store even though the parameter value already exists on entry.
preconditions: The body is a coroutine/async body that StateTransform actually transforms (old_yield_ty is Some).
StateTransform has computed transform.remap entries for argument locals, mapping some arguments to coroutine saved fields.
There may be a resume point whose resume_arg is CTX_ARG itself, so a resume move must be skipped when source and destination coincide.
The coroutine may be movable or immovable, and panic=abort or panic=unwind; tests should cover both.
The inserted argument-to-field assignments must occur at the start of START_BLOCK without renumbering `_2` or corrupting local declarations.
pitfalls: Do not assume MIR parameters are explicitly assigned on function entry. The patch states: "MIR parameters are not explicitly assigned-to when entering the MIR body. If we want to save their values inside the coroutine state, we need to do so explicitly."
Do not renumber or rename the resume local `_2`/CTX_ARG to make it look like a saved local; that was the removed trick and it obscures the fact that a parameter is being stored.

Do not emit a resume move when `point.resume_arg` is already CTX_ARG; guard with `point.resume_arg != CTX_ARG.into()` to avoid a pointless/incorrect move when source and destination are the same local.
Handle all remapped args, not just the resume argument; the new logic iterates `body.args_iter()` and filters by `transform.remap[local]`.

The `CoroutineSavedLocal` debug format was changed to `_s{}` specifically to distinguish saved locals from ordinary MIR locals; test expectations that show `_0`, `_1` are stale, not evidence of a pass regression.
Inline test diffs in this PR are downstream consequences of the changed StateTransform MIR shape (local numbering/parameter use), not evidence that Inline's own rewrite rule changed.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a MIR dump test with `-Zmir-opt-level=0` and `EMIT_MIR ...StateTransform.after.mir` for a coroutine that takes an argument, yields twice, and reads/clones that argument after both yields, plus a `#[track_caller]` variant (the new `tests/mir-opt/building/coroutine.rs` does exactly this with `|arg: String| { yield ("first", arg.clone(), Location::caller()); yield ("second", arg.clone(), Location::caller()); }`). Inspect the after-MIR to verify (a) `_2` remains the argument and `debug _task_context => _2;` rather than a renamed local, (b) the start block explicitly stores the argument into the coroutine field, e.g. `(((*_19) as variant#4).0: std::string::String) = move _2;`, and (c) no bogus resume move is emitted where resume_arg is CTX_ARG. Also update/check coroutine_tiny, async_await, async closures, and panic-abort/panic-unwind MIR expectations; verify saved-local names use `_s{}`.
evidence: StateTransform: Do not renumber resume local.
MIR parameters are not explicitly assigned-to when entering the MIR body.
If we want to save their values inside the coroutine state, we need to do so explicitly.
